title: The chat route emits a six-field remediation contract and the surface renders one sentence: toolRemedy, toolDisclosure, toolRiskClass, connectorRefusal and relayTools reach no component
why_open: apps/web/src/app/api/ai/chat/route.ts returns `connectorRefusal` (:375), `connectorDetail` (:376), `toolRefusal` (:380), `toolDisclosure` (:384), `toolRemedy` (:389) and `toolRiskClass` (:393) plus a whole `relayTools` decision block (:397+). The only consumer reads FOUR of them: apps/web/src/components/ai/TenureAIPanel.tsx:141-146 passes `{answer, aiEnabled, aiDisabledReason, toolRefusal, sourceCount}` into `relayReply`, and apps/web/src/components/ai/relay-reply.ts:20-33 declares `RelayReplyInput` with exactly those four fields — no `toolRemedy`, no `toolDisclosure`, no `connectorRefusal`. So relay-reply.ts:66-72 renders `I wasn't able to search your workspace for this. ${input.toolRefusal}` and stops: a dead end in front of a human, while the machine-readable way out sits unread in the response body. The ledger says this itself at docs/implementation/universal-work-graph-execution-ledger.md:832-837 — "nothing renders toolRemedy yet ... those components are owned by the Connection Center run (WRK-110-002) this session; the wiring is a UI change, not an external blocker." The renderer already exists and is already imported: apps/web/src/components/connections/MissingConnectionCard.tsx takes `capability`, `pendingIntent`, `onAskAdmin`, `onConnect`, and TenureAIPanel.tsx:305 already mounts it — but only on the unconfigured/disabled branch, never on a refusal. `pendingIntent` (MissingConnectionCard.tsx:27-32) is the resumption slot and TenureAIPanel never passes the question that was refused.
smallest_real_change: Widen `RelayReplyInput` (relay-reply.ts:20-33) with the fields the route already sends — `toolRemedy: RelayRemedy | null`, `toolDisclosure: ToolDisclosure | null`, `connectorRefusal: string | null` — and split `RelayOutcome` "retrieval-refused" into the two the remedy already distinguishes: `retrieval-refused-module` (MODULE_NOT_INSTALLED) and `retrieval-refused-permission` (PERMISSION_NOT_HELD), adding `connector-unavailable` for `connectorRefusal`. WIDENING CHECK — `RelayReplyInput` has exactly two construction sites: TenureAIPanel.tsx:141 and relay-reply.test.ts; make the new fields REQUIRED so tsc names both, and fix TenureAIPanel.tsx:141-146 to pass `data.toolRemedy ?? null`, `data.toolDisclosure ?? null`, `data.connectorRefusal ?? null` in the same change. Then return a `remedy` on `RelayReply` and have TenureAIPanel render `MissingConnectionCard` for a refused outcome, building the `CapabilityState` from the remedy (a MODULE_NOT_INSTALLED remedy is `certified:false` -> `resolveCapability` yields NOT_CERTIFIED and therefore NO connect button, which is the rule capability-resolution.ts:5-12 exists to keep; a PERMISSION_NOT_HELD remedy is `certified:true, configured:true, connectableBy:'admin'` -> NEEDS_ADMIN, whose `owner` line names who to ask) and passing the refused question as `pendingIntent` so the work is kept. TESTS TO PROVE: extend relay-reply.test.ts so the SAME `toolRefusal` string with the two different remedy kinds yields two different outcomes — MUTATION: drop the remedy from the branch so both collapse to one outcome, confirm it reds. Add a TenureAIPanel-level assertion (or an apps/web/e2e spec against the existing AI panel) that a PERMISSION_NOT_HELD response renders `[data-connection-outcome="NEEDS_ADMIN"]` and echoes the asked question — MUTATION: stop passing `pendingIntent`, confirm the echo assertion reds. Assert on what the PANEL renders from a real route response shape, never on `relayReply` called with a hand-built object only.

title: Sign-in throws the task away at 32 guarded entry points, and one component already links to a `?next=` the sign-in page does not read
why_open: apps/web/src/app/signin/page.tsx:27 reads searchParams for `error` and NOTHING else; :34 hardcodes `redirectTo: "/dashboard"` inside the dev-login server action; :22 sends an already-signed-in visitor to /dashboard regardless of where they were headed. Meanwhile apps/web/src/components/documents/DocumentViewerOverlay.tsx:407 already renders `href={`/signin?next=${encodeURIComponent(`/orgs/${slug}/documents`)}`}` — a link that is a lie today, because nothing on the sign-in page consumes `next`. Thirty-two guarded entry points discard the destination with a bare `redirect("/signin")`: apps/web/src/app/(app)/layout.tsx:27 and apps/web/src/lib/admin/guard.ts:20 are the two chokepoints, plus dashboard/page.tsx:35, calendar/page.tsx:53, calendar/[id]/page.tsx:22, messages/[id]/page.tsx:61, orgs/[slug]/finance/page.tsx:29, orgs/[slug]/documents/[id]/view/page.tsx:26, search/page.tsx:28, settings/page.tsx:26 and :379, resources/[slug]/page.tsx:22, reports/finance/page.tsx:25, inbox/page.tsx:87, notifications/page.tsx:12 and the rest. There is no return-path helper anywhere: `grep -rn "safeReturnPath|signInPathFor|callbackUrl" apps/web/src` returns only that one DocumentViewerOverlay href. So a member who follows an emailed link to /orgs/x/finance signs in and lands on the dashboard — the exact 'interruption and exact safe task resumption' WRK-030-003 names.
smallest_real_change: Add apps/web/src/lib/http/return-path.ts beside internal-headers.ts with `signInPathFor(pathname, search?)` returning `/signin?next=<encoded>` and `safeReturnPath(raw: string | string[] | undefined): string` that returns '/dashboard' unless the value is a same-origin app path: must start with a single '/', must NOT start with '//' or '/\\', must not match /^[a-z][a-z0-9+.-]*:/i, must not be '/signin' (a loop), and must be decoded ONCE and then re-validated so '%2f%2fevil.test' cannot slip through. Call `signInPathFor` from the two chokepoints — apps/web/src/app/(app)/layout.tsx:27 and apps/web/src/lib/admin/guard.ts:20 (both are `async` and can read `headers()` for the current path) — and in apps/web/src/app/signin/page.tsx read `next` from the searchParams the page ALREADY awaits at :27, replace the hardcoded `redirectTo: "/dashboard"` at :34 with `safeReturnPath(next)`, and make :22's already-signed-in redirect use the same value. NOTE THE §16 RULE: the sign-in page's `redirect()` is not inside a tenant scope, and `signInPathFor` must be called BEFORE `redirect()`, not inside a `withTenantScope` body — tests/architecture/redirect-lives-outside-tenant-scope.test.mjs already enforces that and must stay green. TESTS TO PROVE: a unit table in return-path.test.ts over `//evil.test`, `https://evil.test`, `/\\evil.test`, `%2f%2fevil.test`, `java%0ascript:alert(1)`, `/signin`, `['a','b']`, undefined, and a legitimate `/orgs/consulting/finance` — the first eight collapse to '/dashboard', the last survives. MUTATION: make `safeReturnPath` return `raw` unchanged; the open-redirect rows must red. Then an apps/web/e2e spec: signed out, visit /orgs/<slug>/finance, assert the URL became /signin?next=..., sign in with the dev-login form, assert the final URL is /orgs/<slug>/finance. MUTATION: restore `redirectTo: "/dashboard"`; the e2e must red. That e2e is the one that proves the PRODUCER, not the helper.

title: Execution-time reauthorization has no caller, its idempotency default digest is the empty string, and no approval records the definition version it was raised under
why_open: TWO defects, one file area. (1) apps/web/src/lib/commands/bus.ts:104 declares `options: { requestDigest: string; idempotencyTtlMs?: number } = { requestDigest: "" }`. A caller that omits options claims the idempotency key with digest "", so bus.ts:199 `replayable(claim.existing, options.requestDigest)` compares "" against "" and returns TRUE for a genuinely DIFFERENT request that reused the key — the exact outcome the comment at bus.ts:194 says must not happen. And `dispatch` reauthorizes at execution (the `ports.authorize` call) but has no production caller at all: `grep -rn "lib/commands" apps/web/src` returns nothing outside bus.ts and bus.test.ts. (2) The approval path has the opposite gap and IS reachable: packages/workflow/src/definition.ts:59 gives every `WorkflowDefinition` a `version`, apps/web/src/lib/workflows/approval-definition.ts publishes the pilot's flow through `publishDefinition`, and apps/web/src/lib/approvals.ts:12 drives it — but apps/web/prisma/schema.prisma:464-500 stores NO definition version and no plan digest on `ApprovalRequest`, and neither `availableActions` (approvals.ts:394) nor `nextStatus` (approvals.ts:439) compares the definition a request was raised under with the one deciding it. So editing approval-definition.ts silently re-routes every in-flight request, which is precisely the 'invalidate approval after meaningful plan change' this requirement asks for.
smallest_real_change: (a) Delete the `= { requestDigest: "" }` default at bus.ts:104 so `options` is required, and refuse an empty/whitespace `requestDigest` with a `validation` ContractError BEFORE the idempotency claim is made — an empty digest is not a digest, and a caller with none must be made to say so. WIDENING CHECK: `dispatch` has exactly two call sites, both in bus.test.ts; tsc names them. Prove with a bus.test.ts case that claims a key with digest 'A' then dispatches the same key with digest 'B' and asserts `idempotency.key-reused` rather than a replayed success — MUTATION: restore the `""` default and call dispatch without options; it must red. (b) The reachable half, with NO schema change: `ApprovalRequest.metadata` is already `Json @default("{}")` (schema.prisma:483), so stamp `metadata.definitionVersion = APPROVAL_DEFINITION.version` when a request is submitted in apps/web/src/lib/approvals.ts, and make the decision path refuse with a named refusal when the stored version disagrees with the definition now loaded — the approval must be returned to the requester rather than decided under a flow it was never raised against. That is a real production caller for the invariant and touches no owned file. TESTS TO PROVE: an approvals test that submits under version X, bumps `APPROVAL_DEFINITION.version` to Y, and asserts the decide path refuses — MUTATION: drop the version comparison and confirm it reds; a second test asserting a request submitted and decided under the SAME version still advances, so the guard is not simply blocking everything. Assert on what the approvals decision path EMITS, not on a version-compare helper called directly. STATED CONSTRAINT: this deliberately uses `metadata` instead of a new column so apps/web/prisma/schema.prisma is not written by two concurrent runs; a proper column is the follow-up.

title: Relationships carry no provenance, no confidence and no review expiry, and no production code ever constructs one — the whole ReBAC branch of the engine is unreachable
why_open: packages/authorization/src/relationships.ts:62-72 defines `Relationship` as type/fromPrincipalId/tenantId/one target plus `Dated` only: there is no provenance discriminator, no confidence, no reviewedAt and no review expiry, so an edge inferred from a roster join is indistinguishable from one a Director asserted. `relationshipHoldsAt` (relationships.ts:111-119) therefore treats an unreviewed inference as permanent authority the moment it has no end date — the failure the file's own comment at :57-60 argues against for end dates. Worse, the branch is unreachable: packages/authorization/src/decide.ts:68 declares `relationships?: readonly Relationship[]` OPTIONAL, and the four readers at decide.ts:289, :296, :307 and :434 all fall back to `world.relationships ?? []`, while the ONLY production constructors of an AuthorizationWorld — apps/web/src/lib/authz/seat-world.ts:88-98 (`seatWorld`) and :180 (`institutionWorld`, which spreads `base`) — return `{principals, memberships, roles, grants, enabledModules, entitlements}` with no `relationships` key at all. `grep -rn "relationships" apps/web/src` returns NOTHING. This is the silent-optional-field failure mode exactly: tsc is happy, every packages/authorization test passes because those tests build worlds with relationships in them, and in the running app MANAGES / ADVISES / OWNS / OVERSEES / PARTICIPATES_IN decide nothing.
smallest_real_change: Add a REQUIRED `provenance: { origin: 'ASSERTED' | 'INFERRED' | 'IMPORTED'; source: string; confidence: number; reviewedAt: string | null; reviewExpiresAt: string | null }` to `Relationship` (relationships.ts:62), extend `relationshipProblems` (relationships.ts:87) with `CONFIDENCE_OUT_OF_RANGE` and `ASSERTED_WITHOUT_REVIEW`, and make `relationshipHoldsAt` (relationships.ts:111) return false for an INFERRED edge whose `reviewExpiresAt` has passed or whose confidence is below a stated floor — an unreviewed inference decays instead of becoming permanent authority. WIDENING CHECK, and it is the whole risk here: because the field is REQUIRED, run `grep -rn 'type: "MANAGES"\|type: "ADVISES"\|type: "OWNS"\|type: "OVERSEES"\|type: "PARTICIPATES_IN"\|type: "COLLABORATES_WITH"\|type: "HOLDS_SEAT_IN"' packages apps` and fix EVERY construction site in the same change — today those are packages/authorization/src/relationships.test.ts, rebac-assurance.test.ts and decide.ts's own tests, so the blast radius is small and provable. Then give the branch its missing production caller: add `relationshipsFor(ctx, tenantId)` to apps/web/src/lib/authz/seat-world.ts deriving INFERRED edges from data getUserContext already loads (rbac.ts) — HOLDS_SEAT_IN from each live orgRole with `source:'RoleAssignment'`, OVERSEES from each institutionRole with `source:'InstitutionMembership'` — each stamped `origin:'INFERRED'`, a confidence and a `reviewExpiresAt`, and include it in BOTH the `seatWorld` return at seat-world.ts:88 AND the `institutionWorld` return at :180. That second site is the consumer a widening would otherwise miss: it spreads `base` and overrides `grants`, so it inherits relationships only if `seatWorld` sets them — assert that explicitly. MUTATION TO PROVE: delete the `relationships` key from `seatWorld`'s return only — a `decide()` test that grants a permission through a HOLDS_SEAT_IN edge must red through BOTH seatWorld and institutionWorld; restore and both pass. Second mutation: set an INFERRED edge's `reviewExpiresAt` into the past and assert the permission is refused, proving decay is real and not a declared field.

title: Retention and legal hold exist as a library apps/web never calls, and every derived record — MemoryRecord written from an outbox event — survives the deletion of the thing it describes
why_open: packages/audit/src/retention.ts is a complete retention/legal-hold planner (`RetentionPolicy` :68, `LegalHold` :45, `HeldRecord` :76, `RetentionPlan` :92-105, `applyRetention` :169, chain anchors so a cut stays verifiable). Its ONLY caller is apps/system-studio/src/lib/audit-ledger.ts:284, which plans retention over the STUDIO control-plane ledger — a different store, in a package this run does not own. Inside apps/web there is nothing: `grep -rn "applyRetention|LegalHold|RetentionPlan" apps/web` returns ZERO hits, so the tenant `AuditEvent` table (apps/web/prisma/schema.prisma:1335) grows forever, no institution can place a hold, and no deletion is ever planned. The propagation half is worse because it is now reachable: apps/web/src/lib/outbox/consumers.ts writes a `MemoryRecord` from an `ApprovalDecided` event, deriving its title and content from the `ApprovalRequest` row it names — and nothing removes or tombstones that derived record when the approval is deleted. schema.prisma:464 gives ApprovalRequest `onDelete: Cascade` from Organization, so deleting an organization takes its approvals and leaves the MemoryRecords that quote them. WRK-070-004's 'propagation across graph, chunks, embeddings, caches, summaries, and citations' has no mechanism for the one derived artefact the platform actually produces.
smallest_real_change: Do the propagation half first, because it is small, reachable and provable, and leave the AuditEvent retention job as the second step. (1) `MemoryRecord` rows written by apps/web/src/lib/outbox/consumers.ts already name their source approval; make that link explicit and queryable by writing the source id into the record the consumer creates, and add a `propagateDeletion(tx, {kind:'ApprovalRequest', id})` in a new apps/web/src/lib/retention.ts that removes or tombstones every derived MemoryRecord for a deleted source. Its production caller is the approval-deletion path — and if none exists, the honest caller is a new pass in the outbox job route (apps/web/src/app/api/jobs/outbox/route.ts is the model: JOB_SECRET bearer check, `parseJobRequest`, `forEachInstitution`) that reconciles orphaned derived records per tenant. (2) Add `apps/web/src/app/api/jobs/retention/route.ts` modelled on apps/web/src/app/api/jobs/slo/route.ts, calling `applyRetention` from @tenure/audit per institution over `AuditEvent` and REPORTING the plan (expire / retain / heldBack / chainBlocked counts and the anchors) without deleting anything — `applyRetention` plans a deletion and never performs one (packages/audit/src/index.ts:30 says so), and a reported plan is a real caller that a later step can act on. TESTS TO PROVE: an .itest against the running Postgres (docker ps shows it up) that seeds an approval, runs the outbox pass so the MemoryRecord is written, deletes the approval, runs the propagation pass, and asserts the derived record is gone — MUTATION: make `propagateDeletion` a no-op; it must red. A second .itest that places a legal hold covering the seeded tenant's audit rows and asserts the retention endpoint reports them in `heldBack`, not `expire` — MUTATION: pass `[]` for holds at the ROUTE's call site (not inside applyRetention) and confirm it reds, which is what proves the producer rather than the library. TEARDOWN RULE: the fixture must delete only ids it created — do not claim the pilot slug and do not delete a seeded institution.

title: Versioned include/exclude resource selectors and impact diffs do not exist in any form: a connection's scope is all-or-nothing and a scope change shows nobody what it would change
why_open: `grep -rn 'Selector|selector' packages/provisioning/src packages/module-runtime/src apps/web/src/lib` returns only a CSS-parsing test and a Unicode range comment — there is no `ResourceSelector`, no include/exclude list, no selector version and no impact diff anywhere in the tree. packages/provisioning/src/catalogs.ts models a connector's egress hosts, capabilities, certification and (since WRK-040-003 landed) `providerReview` with `requestedScopes` — the SCOPE it asks the provider for — but nothing models WHICH RESOURCES inside a connected workspace are in scope: `ConnectorEntry` has no selector field, and apps/web/src/lib/connections/capability-resolution.ts:16-22 says so in its own words ("it does not model a provider connection record: Connection, ConnectionOpportunity, PendingActionIntent and ConnectionLaunchToken exist in no package and no migration"). Because selectors are unversioned and absent, the impact-diff half has nothing to diff: there is no way to answer 'if I remove this folder from the selection, which indexed objects and which citations stop being reachable', which is the question WRK-020-002 exists to make answerable before someone clicks Save.
smallest_real_change: Add packages/provisioning/src/resource-selector.ts declaring `ResourceSelector { version: number; include: readonly ResourcePattern[]; exclude: readonly ResourcePattern[] }` where a pattern is `{ kind: 'container' | 'object'; externalId: string; recursive: boolean }`, with `selectorProblems` refusing an empty include set (an empty include is 'everything' to one reader and 'nothing' to another, the same single-valuedness argument relationships.ts:79-85 makes for TWO_TARGETS), refusing an exclude that no include could ever match (dead rule), and refusing a version that did not increase. Then `selectorDiff(previous, next, known: readonly ResourceRef[])` returning `{ added, removed, unchanged }` over a caller-supplied set of known resources — EXCLUDE ALWAYS WINS over include, stated once here rather than re-derived per surface. Give it a real caller in the same change, or it is dead code: add `selector?: ResourceSelector` to `ConnectorEntry` (catalogs.ts:194) and extend `isUsable` (catalogs.ts:393) with a new `UsabilityReason` `selector-invalid` so a connector whose selection does not parse cannot reach an availability decision — `availabilityDecisions` (catalogs.ts:562) is already rendered per connector, so the refusal reaches a surface. WIDENING CHECK: keep `selector` OPTIONAL on `ConnectorEntry` (the 24 PLANNED provider packs in packages/provisioning/src/provider-packs.ts are construction sites and none of them selects anything yet) but make `isUsable` refuse a PUBLISHED connector that HAS a selector which does not parse — the gate is on the value, not on its presence. TESTS TO PROVE, all in catalogs.test.ts / resource-selector.test.ts: exclude-beats-include on an overlapping pair; a diff that reports a removal when a folder leaves `include`; `selector-invalid` reaching an `availabilityDecisions` row. MUTATION: make exclude lose to include and confirm both the precedence test and the diff test red; MUTATION: drop `selector-invalid` from `isUsable` and confirm the availability-decision test reds — assert on what `availabilityDecisions` EMITS, never on `selectorProblems` alone.
